pages.text: Dark blueberries were ripe near the forest floor. They hung in clusters on every bush.
Nils wanted a big bucket full to eat with milk that evening. Grandpa took his little bucket.
"I want a big bucket!" Nils dragged one as big as Grandpa from the shed.
Nils picked berries into it. They barely covered the bottom. "A long way to go."
The bucket grew heavier. Nils dragged it between the bushes.
Bump! It caught on a tree root. Out tumbled blueberries onto the moss.
The spilled berries rolled into mossy gaps and hid. Only a few remained in the bucket. His hands were all purple.
Without a word, Grandpa put his little bucket in front of Nils.
The little bucket filled quickly. Nils poured it into the big bucket. Now the big bucket was full!
That evening, bowls were full of blueberries in milk. Purple stained both Nils's and Grandpa's mouths.
